title: Anita Somani Wins Third Ohio House Term With 70.79 Percent of Vote
excerpt: The Indian American obstetrician-gynecologist defeated Republican Kelly Hunter-Kalagidis by 20,738 votes in District 8, her strongest showing in three elections.
body:
• Dr Anita Somani, an Indian American obstetrician-gynecologist, won re-election to the Ohio House of Representatives with 70.79% of the vote in unofficial results.
  • She defeated Republican Kelly Hunter-Kalagidis by 20,738 votes in Franklin County's District 8, where all 81 precincts had reported.
  • It is her third consecutive general-election win — 56% in 2022 and 64.5% in 2024 — and her new two-year term begins in January 2027.
  • Results remain unofficial until state certification.

Dr Anita Somani, the Indian American physician who has represented parts of the Columbus area in the Ohio House since 2023, has won a third consecutive term, defeating Republican challenger Kelly Hunter-Kalagidis in the state's 8th House District. According to unofficial results reported by Ohio election authorities and covered by The American Bazaar, Somani took 70.79% of the vote, a margin of 20,738 votes, with all 81 precincts in the district reported in the Franklin County summary. The results are unofficial until state certification.

A rising vote share across three cycles

Somani, a Democrat, first entered electoral politics in 2022, winning an open seat in Ohio's 11th House District with 56% of the vote against Republican Omar Tarazi. After redistricting, she contested District 8 in 2024 and won with 64.5% against Aaron Neumann. Her 70.79% this year is her strongest showing yet. Her new two-year term begins in January 2027, and her official Ohio House member page lists her committee and legislative work for the current assembly.

From the clinic to the Statehouse

Somani is a first-generation immigrant from India. According to her official Ohio Statehouse biography, her father was the first Asian person to serve in an Ohio governor's cabinet. She has practised as an obstetrician-gynecologist at OhioHealth in Columbus for more than three decades, earned her medical degree from the Medical College of Ohio, completed her residency at Mount Carmel Medical Center in Columbus, and holds certification in minimally invasive gynecologic surgery. Before elected office she was co-chair of the Physicians Action Network, Ohio state director for South Asians for America, and served on the boards of the Columbus Medical Association and Planned Parenthood of Central Ohio.

Her legislative record

In the legislature, Somani serves on the House Medicaid Committee and is the ranking Democratic member of the House Health Committee. Her sponsored measures, per her official record as summarised by The American Bazaar, include House Bill 128, the Reproductive Care Act; House Bill 237, aimed at protecting access to assisted reproduction including IVF; legislation on menopause and hormone-therapy coverage; and House Bill 337, proposing trigger-lock requirements for firearm sales. Sponsorship is not enactment — those bills are proposals she has championed, working in a chamber Republicans continue to control, though Democrats reduced the Republican supermajority in the 2026 state elections.

What comes next

Somani's next term is expected to centre on the healthcare portfolio she has built: reproductive health, IVF access and women's health. For Ohio's Indian American community — one of the professional communities concentrated around Columbus, Dublin and Worthington, the areas her district covers — she remains one of the most visible Indian-origin state legislators in the Midwest, and one whose margin has grown in every cycle she has contested.
